title: Sum of Two Numbers
statement:
Given two integers a and b, compute their sum.

Input
A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.

Output
Print a single integer — the value of a + b.

Constraints
-1,000,000,000 <= a, b <= 1,000,000,000

Example
Input:
1000000 2000000
Output:
3000000

The two values are read from standard input; anything your program writes to standard output is compared against the expected answer (trailing whitespace and a trailing newline are ignored).

title: Reverse a String
statement:
Given a string s, print it with its characters in reverse order.

Input
A single line containing the string s. It consists of printable ASCII characters and has no leading or trailing spaces.

Output
Print s reversed, on one line.

Constraints
1 <= length of s <= 1000

Example
Input:
hello
Output:
olleh

A palindrome such as "racecar" reverses to itself.

title: FizzBuzz (1..N)
statement:
Print the integers from 1 to N, one per line, with three substitutions:

  - for a multiple of 3 (but not 5), print "Fizz" instead of the number;
  - for a multiple of 5 (but not 3), print "Buzz" instead of the number;
  - for a multiple of both 3 and 5, print "FizzBuzz".

Input
A single line containing one integer N.

Output
Exactly N lines. Line i holds either i or its Fizz / Buzz / FizzBuzz substitution.

Constraints
1 <= N <= 10000

Example
Input:
5
Output:
1
2
Fizz
4
Buzz

title: Maximum of an Array
statement:
Given an array of n integers, print the largest value it contains.

Input
The first line contains a single integer n — the number of elements.
The second line contains n space-separated integers.

Output
Print a single integer — the maximum element of the array.

Constraints
1 <= n <= 100000
-1,000,000,000 <= each element <= 1,000,000,000

Example
Input:
5
3 1 4 1 5
Output:
5

All values may be negative, in which case the answer is the one closest to zero — e.g. [-3, -1, -7, -2] has maximum -1.
